rule: No new CSS or inline background/border/box-shadow surface paint outside registered chrome primitives.

entries.selector: /* "New version available" prompt — quiet, fixed, non-blocking. Shown only after a newer build is detected (src/net/appUpdate.ts). */ .app-update-banner
/* − / + pixel steppers beside a slider — same plate as the reset, with a fixed width so a row of [−][slider][+][↺] stays tidy. */ .pages-step

/* Account menu — small kit panel-framed popover anchored under the avatar. A minimal one-line row: the username + the door (the door IS the sign-out, no text label — the bar avatar already carries identity). */ .account-menu

/* ADR-0082: these are the real DOM ancestors shown by Chrome Audit. Legacy feature classes may still own layout, spacing, and copy treatment, but every house-chrome frame is painted by the registered inner role. Keeping this contract after the feature rules also prevents a local raw-CSS background or one-pixel border from silently winning over the installed Chrome family. */ :is(.level-editor-screen, .skirmish-screen, .chrome-family-surface) .inner-box
/* An inspector property whose value is a link into the Glossary (e.g. Layering). */ .tileset-inline-link

/* Army-wide display layers from the in-match shortcut grid. Side-coded: player = cool blue/green, enemy = warm magenta/red. Declared before .is-threat / .is-move so the focused-piece cyan and the enemy danger-zone red win where layers overlap a cell. */ .skirmish-board-cell-hit.is-player-move::before

/* Campaign battle result — a modal over the board when a campaign level is won or lost. Layout only: the panel itself wears the shared baked-skin .settings-frame, and the buttons are the standard .app-header-button chrome. */ .campaign-result
/* Canonical Level Editor dropdown: HouseSelect owns the shared frame and chevron. */ .le-select-wrap

/* Chrome Audit is a dense working surface, so secondary copy and native menus need stronger contrast than catalog metadata. Keep the palette dark without making labels, current values, or the expanded OS-level select menu recede. */ .chrome-lab-controls
/* Completed widgets gallery (/design/widgets) */ /* Catalog / Glossary toggle */ .catalog-mode-toggle a, .catalog-mode-toggle .active
/* Crest: transparent PNG cropped from the approved render by normalize-main-menu-profile.mjs. */ .profile-crest

/* Drag-to-move diagnostic: the square hit-testing thinks the cursor is over, even when that square is not a legal destination. The green valid-drop style below overrides it. */ .skirmish-board-cell-hit.is-drop-aim::before

/* Drag-to-move: the legal square the held piece is hovering over. Declared last so it wins over .is-move / :hover on the same cell — a bright green "drop here" fill + ring. */ .skirmish-board-cell-hit.is-drop-hover::before
/* Drawn text box → kit line frame (panel-line over its own navy surface, ADR-0032/0034) + role-token inset + ladder gaps (ADR-0055/0056). */ .le-material-values

/* Drawn text boxes wear a kit line frame (ADR-0032/0034): the transparent-interior panel-line 9-slice over the box's own navy surface (a border-box background layer, reaching the frame edge). Ready/blocked swap the SOURCE to the success/warning tone twin — one frame, tone at the corners. Content insets by the role token (ADR-0055). */ .le-status-current

/* Entry-list primitive: an added row that names itself, keeps its knobs behind a caret and can be removed. Shared by the Generate panel's cover sets and the Town panel's buildings, so these are no longer scoped to .le-generate. */ .le-gen-cover
/* Footer = campaign actions: Duplicate + Export neutral, Delete Campaign danger (base .is-danger). */ .ce-import-campaign, .ce-footer .ce-asset-button:not(.is-danger)
/* Frame + icon layers crop their catalog sheet via the --asset-* custom properties emitted by frameStyleForAsset(). */ .mode-button-art, .mode-button-9slice, .mode-button-icon

/* Frame the clock config as the same baked stone panel the settings rows wear (panel-line over the stone surface), so it reads as a real framed control on the page rather than text floating on the scene. Content matches .settings-row's inset. */ .skirmish-setup-clock

/* Higher specificity than `.tileset-control-stack button` (which forces min-height:34/padding:8-10), so these stay tiny icon buttons that fit inside the h3's natural height instead of growing it. */ .tileset-filter-group-head .tileset-filter-group-actions button
/* Icon-based tab glyphs — reused curated kit icons (ADR-0011/0032), full-colour on the dark panel like the count-pip rooks. Sized to sit inside the 44px kit frame. */ .skirmish-tab-icon

/* Inner chrome role: buttons, toggles, selects, text wells, and small line boxes inherit the same rail weight instead of each component tuning its own pixels. */ .level-editor-screen .settings-chrome-button, .level-editor-screen .settings-toggle, .level-editor-screen .settings-stepper .settings-chrome-button
/* Isolated specimen capture surface — one component per page, for exact screenshots */ .specimen-capture
/* Live component specimens on the design portfolio */ .portfolio-specimen

/* Marquee selection highlight for the Generate/Tile scope. TileGrid's flat overlay cell is already seated at the top edge of the surface diamond, so this begins at 0 rather than applying the terrain-frame equator offset again. Keeping it in that 10k overlay band makes north/west scenic coordinates visible above the terrain canvas while structures remain above it. */ .le-region-cell
/* Move-tool variants of the tile-ring: the held unit's cell, and a can/can't-drop destination. */ .tileset-cell-ring.is-move-from
/* No board box: the board container paints NO background — the board art floats on the screen's night-sky background (ADR-0032). A tinted rectangle here is the "box". */ .skirmish-board-lab

/* No box: the words float. This readout is pinned in the header and never moves, so it needs no surface to sit on — drop the per-row LINE frame + stone fill that .settings-row bakes in, and the padding that cleared the frame. The locked height stays as an invisible reserve (sized for label + artist + title) so the soundtrack list below never jerks when the title flips between "Nothing" and a playing track. */ .settings-nowplaying-row
/* Per-focus layer-visibility toggle (the "vision" eye). Amber when the layer is hidden, so it's obvious the board is concealing something rather than empty. */ .tileset-vision-toggle
/* Point at the clean, method-forged kit glyphs (transparent, no baked box) instead of the contact-sheet slices (ADR-0011/0032). menu + rook have no forged twin yet. */ .skirmish-icon-flag
/* Portrait-candidate cards show the accepted HUD crop (square), not the full-body master. */ .studio-portrait-crop

/* Premoves (queued while the opponent thinks). Cool indigo, distinct from the live-turn cyan move highlight: -target = a square the selected piece could be premoved to, -premove = a square already queued as a step in the chain. */ .skirmish-board-cell-hit.is-premove-target::before
/* Profile / status panel — live DOM component (element 03) */ .menu-panel

/* Shared frame primitive. One panel.png 9-slice with a SINGLE corner-size token, so every settings frame's gold corner brackets render at the same scale no matter how thick or padded the individual frame is. Per-frame classes below layer only layout (grid/padding/size) on top — they must NOT redeclare the border, or the corners desync again (which is exactly the bug this replaces: header/rail/main each set their own 9/18/24px border, scaling the shared 36px corner three ways). */ .settings-frame

/* Strip the default .tileset-view-stage box (checkerboard fill + border + radius) on both in-game boards: the live skirmish board AND the level editor. They share the same world background, so they must read identically — the editor board floats on the night sky too, not on the studio's transparency-checker stage (ADR-0032). */ .skirmish-board-lab .tileset-view-stage, .level-editor-screen .tileset-view-stage

/* Studio/dev editor & inspector surfaces (Portrait Editor, Doodad Editor, Surface Lab, Artwork/Tile Compare) on the standard title bar (ADR-0004/0023): a full-bleed bar on top, the existing tool body filling and scrolling in the row below it. The shell runs .is-immersive so the global topbar is hidden and .app-root is full-bleed. */ .dev-editor-screen
/* Surface catalog swatch — the texture tiled, the way it fills a panel behind chrome. */ .surface-swatch

/* Test in the always-visible Actions dock: a full-width primary button so it reads as the editor's "test this board now" verb, distinct from the Undo/Redo icons above it. */ .le-actions-dock .le-play-board

/* The board-link field wears the kit `field-input` 9-slice (its own navy well is the frame's fill slice), never a hand-rolled border (ADR-0032/0034) — the same input chrome the Codex editor uses. Single-line control: horizontal inset on the role token, vertical centring from min-height (ADR-0055). */ .le-board-link-input
/* The campaign-name field (Campaign › Name row) — the kit field-input 9-slice. */ .ce-name-input
/* The door is the action — a bare icon button (no fabricated surface), labelled for screen readers + a hover tooltip, brightening on hover/focus. */ .account-menu-exit

/* The field is stripped separately from the frame, because the guard above is aimed at a raw-CSS background — not at a box whose own INSTALLED image is the point of it. A unit portrait's painted scene arrives from the drawable catalog and is part of the portrait, so stripping it left every framed bust (the roster thumbnails, the Selected Unit seat) on flat fill while the same unit's unframed portrait kept its scene. */ :is(.level-editor-screen, .skirmish-screen, .chrome-family-surface) .inner-box:not(.has-backdrop)

/* The live viewer's stage is a bare viewport here: strip the Studio stage's box (10px padding, border, transparency checkerboard) so the board floats on the night-sky backdrop above — the checkerboard is banned from board/level previews (ADR-0067). */ .ce-level-viewer .tileset-view-stage
/* The name doubles as the edit trigger — a bare button that reads as plain text and brightens on hover/focus so it's discoverable as clickable. */ .account-menu-name-button

/* The on-board zone overlay: a translucent tinted diamond. It COPIES the selection ring's seating exactly — top: --iso-tile-surface-top + the diamond clip-path — so it sits on the tile EQUATOR (y69), never at iso-tile-height/2. That equator seating is the fix for the recurring "board overlay diamonds sit too low" bug (see .tileset-cell-ring). z-index below the selection ring (3) so a selected zoned tile still shows its ring on top. */ .le-zone-cell
/* The two darkening scrims the old pseudo stacked over the scene — now a layer ABOVE the animated regions, so moving water is darkened like the art around it. */ .scene-backdrop-scrim

/* Tier selector (category / surface / focus / process / tool / option) — one tight joined segmented control on a SINGLE row, never the fat two-row button stack. This is the instrument-grade density the spec calls for, and it is the ONE segmented-control primitive: Catalog tiers and every Lab selector use it. */ .tileset-tier-seg
/* Trailing rule that runs from the eyebrow to the panel edge, matching the concept. */ .settings-section-title::after

/* Two classes → out-specifies the base card-image checkerboard (pages aren't transparent sprites): a hero shot of the live route, full-bleed. The gradient shows only until the thumbnail loads / if it's missing. */ .tileset-studio-card-image.pages-card-image
/* Zone brush preview (fills the 48px thumb) + the small swatch dot in the zone picker. */ .le-brush-thumb-zone
contained options are regions split by structural dividers. */ .house-select-menu
controls and measurements deliberately live outside it so the image model receives only canonical board pixels plus measured clear space. */ .predrawn-reference-tool
drifts a few px with the clamp()ed gap/padding, imperceptible for a stone texture). ADR-0063. */ .settings-tab
geometry changes never restore a committed public-file fallback. */ .kit-divider

its tone swaps the SOURCE to the success/warning/error twin — the semantic accent that was a raw border-left stripe now lives in the frame's corners. Content insets by the role token (ADR-0055). */ .le-status-entry
keyboard focus keeps a real outline. */ .skirmish-roster-slot.active

only the fluted shaft between them stretches to the thumb's length. Painting the sprite with background-size:100% 100% (the old way) scaled the WHOLE column with the thumb, so a tall thumb — the Unit palette has little to scroll, so its grip is nearly full-height — smeared the caps and the central motif vertically. */ .kit-scroll-thumb
only the frame comes from the kit. */ .le-seg-btn
only the screen name changes. DOM order is brand-then-name, so no reordering is needed. Component: src/ui/shared/BrandLockup. */ .brand-lockup

steps() just advances the frame index. !important clears the global `* { animation: none }` OS-reduce reset (~6477): Windows "animations off" reports prefers-reduced-motion falsely, and ambient scenery must not freeze for those players (deploy-drop/ADR-0048 precedent). The EXPLICIT in-game choice (:root.reduce-motion) does freeze it, to frame 0 = the exact static art. NO image-rendering override: the sheet must be resampled exactly like the scene canvas under it (smooth cover scaling, not pixelated). */ .scene-backdrop-anim
the current state is "lit" (warm wood-light on, cool stone-light off) and the other dims. No raw-CSS chrome to throw away. */ .settings-toggle

the keys still walk the ladder. The BOX is this wrapper, a fixed width so it's identical on every row and the +/- keys line up column-for-column. The input sits borderless inside it, and any unit (e.g. "s") rides INSIDE the same box — putting it outside would widen one row and break alignment. */ .settings-stepper-field
the ornament is the only surface. Because it DRAWS a box around its text, the content insets by the role token (ADR-0055): text never sits flush against the drawn edge. */ .le-violations
the page-specific class adds only content layout (grid columns), never the frame, so the bars match by construction. The in-game HUD is the compact variant of it. */ .app-titlebar
the panel wears the SAME kit panel.png 9-slice as the HUD, and its buttons are the SAME .le-seg-btn kit frames — nothing here is a hand-rolled border (ADR-0002/0011/0014). */ .confirm-scrim
the per-region controls live in the standard tileset-view-controls aside. */ .surface-dressing-main

the SELECTED item is highlighted with a subtle fill + accent bar, the rest stay plain. No per-item frame (the rail panel already carries the gold-bracket chrome). Mirrors the grouped-list content. */ .settings-tab

the studio topbar carries the breadcrumb, so there is no second header. The Surface segmented + provenance live in the shared Controls aside (rendered as a sibling, straight into the shell grid). */ .al-lab-main
this class owns only the title-bar-specific content geometry and interaction layout. */ .titlebar-control
this feature class owns only portrait composition and sizing. The Selected-Unit HUD, roster slots, and editor previews all render through it. */ .unit-portrait
this only advances the frame index via steps() — no visual effect. Per-tuft phase comes from a negative --gc-delay so the field never pulses in unison. */ .gc-tuft
transparent board corners reveal the level world, never a transparency checkerboard (ADR-0067). */ .ce-level-viewer

/* The rail belongs on whichever edge is INTERIOR, and this dock changes which one that is. Docked right, the panel meets the viewport on its right, the title bar on its top and the floor on its bottom, so the offscreen-rails contract reduces its frame to a LEFT rail only. Pinned to the bottom it spans the full width instead: left and right now reach the viewport and the TOP is the one edge facing the board. Left as-is it drew a rail down the side it no longer needs and nothing at all where the board meets it, which is the "just abruptly starts" edge. Same installed frame and the same rail width — only the side moves. Written at the same specificity as the contract it amends, because that rule carries !important. */ :root:has(.app-titlebar.chrome-rails-offscreen) :is(.level-editor-screen, .skirmish-screen) [data-shell-controls-panel][data-controls-mobile="sheet"]::before
